evaluations.bottleneck: Before Graunt's Observations on the Bills of Mortality, population-level mortality patterns were impossible to assess because London's bills existed only as unaggregated weekly counts with no tabulated frequencies or ratios.
Before Halley's Breslau life table, fair pricing of life annuities was impractical because no age-specific mortality probabilities derived from recorded births and deaths existed.
Before The Nautical Almanac, determining longitude at sea by lunar distances was impractical because the required ephemeris positions were not precomputed for sailors to use aboard ship.

Before Quetelet's Sur l'homme, describing a population by a statistical central type was impractical because social and bodily measurements were not yet treated as distributions clustered around an average.
Before Leibniz's differential calculus, systematically optimizing continuous quantities was impractical because no general symbolic notation and algorithmic rules for differentiation existed.
Before Kolmogorov's probability axioms, rigorous reasoning about expectations over arbitrary probability distributions was impractical because probability had no unified measure-theoretic foundation.

Q7.evidence: Kolmogorov's Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (1933) recast probability as measure on a sample space with expectation as integration, and that axiomatic framework became the standard foundation later work builds on without re-deriving it.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if post-1933 probability practice is shown to have proceeded mainly on non-Kolmogorov foundations.
Q7.source: Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (Foundations of the Theory of Probability)

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Mersenne's Académie Parisienne, rapid exchange and criticism of new results among European natural philosophers was impractical because no regular correspondence hub and meeting circle connected them.
Before the Royal Society, validating and disseminating experimental claims was impractical because no chartered institution organized regular meetings, registers of experiments, and publication.
Before the Journal des Sçavans, learning of recent scholarly work was impractical because results circulated only through books and private letters with no periodic review journal.

Before Philosophical Transactions, broadcasting experimental and observational results to a wide readership was impractical because no scientific journal published society proceedings and correspondence.
Before the French Academy of Sciences, sustained state-supported collaborative research was impractical because no salaried national academy employed scientists to work on shared problems.
Before Cardano's Liber de Ludo Aleae, computing fair odds for dice and card games was impractical because outcomes were not enumerated as equally likely cases counted combinatorially.
Before Johan de Witt's life annuity valuation, pricing a life annuity on expected lifetime was impractical because annuity valuation did not combine mortality data with discounted expected payments.
Before Gauss's recovery of Ceres, relocating a lost asteroid from a few observations was impractical because no method combined sparse observations with a probabilistic error model to fit an orbit.
Before Graunt's Bills of Mortality frequency counting, estimating an empirical distribution from records was impractical because events were not aggregated into counts and proportions by category.
Before Simpson's theory of observational errors, reasoning about the accuracy of an averaged observation was impractical because observational errors were not modeled as a probability distribution.

Before Laplace's inverse probability in the Théorie analytique des probabilités, systematic inference from observed data to the probabilities of causes was impractical because inverse probability had no unified analytic treatment.

Before Gibbs's ensemble entropy, quantifying the uncertainty of a probability distribution over microstates was impractical because ensemble theory had no entropy functional defined directly on the distribution itself.

Q6.evidence: Gibbs's Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics (1902) defined ensemble entropy as -sum p_i ln p_i over state probabilities, the exact functional form Shannon generalized in 1948 and whose two-distribution extension is cross-entropy.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if Shannon's 1948 entropy form is shown to have no lineage through statistical-mechanics entropy.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the Pascal-Fermat correspondence, fairly dividing the stakes of an interrupted game was impossible to settle rigorously because no method computed expected outcomes from the combinations of future plays.

Before de Moivre's Doctrine of Chances, computing probabilities for large numbers of trials was impractical because binomial sums had no tractable approximation and probability had no systematic textbook treatment.

Before Bayes's Essay, revising the probability of a cause in light of observed outcomes was impractical because no theorem related a posterior probability to the prior probability and the likelihood of the evidence.
